_comment: Two declared values of one attribute that draw the same picture, with the reason each is accepted.
A row here is NOT permission to leave a defect: `reason` must say why the values CANNOT differ on this platform, or say plainly that the row records a defect and names who owns the fix.

Generated by no tool - written by the lane that owns the platform. `jui conformance gate --value-discrimination` fails on any collapse that is not here, and on any row whose fixture stopped collapsing.

entries.reason: CSS has one truncation, not four. Clip / Middle / Tail all resolve to `text-overflow: ellipsis` + `overflow: hidden` because CSS has no middle-truncation and no clip-without-ellipsis that a still capture can tell apart from ellipsis. rjui maps them deliberately (base_converter lineBreakMode, plan 49 2df3401) and the comment there says so. Char and Word are NOT in this ledger: they map to word-break / overflow-wrap and the gate sees them as distinct, which is the evidence that the mapping is real and only these three collapse.
Same as clip/middle: CSS has one truncation. See that row.
Same as clip/middle: CSS has one truncation. See that row.

The three resizable values draw the SAME grabber. `resize: both | horizontal | vertical` differ only in which axis a drag is allowed on; the corner affordance the browser paints is identical, so a capture taken at rest cannot separate them. rjui emits resize / resize-x / resize-y distinctly (plan 49 2df3401) and `none` IS separated by the gate, which is what shows the mapping is real.
Same as both/horizontal: the grabber is identical across the three resizable values. See that row.
Same as both/horizontal: the grabber is identical across the three resizable values. See that row.

Compose Material defines exactly two text-field chromes - filled (underline) and outlined - where UIKit defines four (none/line/bezel/roundedRect). Both android render paths map the three bordered spellings onto the SAME outlined chrome on purpose: the codegen emits a binary `isOutlined` (textfield_component.rb borderStyle case) and the dynamic renderer resolves the same boolean (DynamicTextFieldComponent.resolveIsOutlined), so codegen and dynamic agree - run 5 parity has NO borderStyle row, only this value gate does. Drawing three distinct android chromes would invent android-only visuals with no Material counterpart and desynchronise the two renderers. `none` is NOT here: it maps to not-outlined and discriminates, which is the evidence the mapping is read at all. Recorded as measured, not blessed: if a ruling later assigns distinct android chromes, these rows go stale and the gate forces them out (plan 49 lane C, run 5).
Same as bezel/line: Material has two chromes, UIKit four. See that row.

entries.owner: E (SSoT) — recorded per 49 ruling; implementation is post-release work
entries.reason: Declared styled face unimplemented, scheduled post-release — the fixture-side counterpart of the six C2/presence-only rows in codegen_effect.json (same family, B's ledger). The boolean face works: presence is read and the line is drawn; only the object face's contents (lineStyle, color, lineOffset) are unread, so {styled} and true draw the same picture BY CONSTRUCTION until styling lands. Do not read this row as 'underline does not work'. The row leaves this ledger when the styled renderer ships and the two pictures separate.
entries.note: android has no row for this pair on purpose: the pair was not compared there (not-both-active) because kjui's dynamic renderer drops the line entirely for the object face — styled renders byte-identical to the CONTROL, a run-5 finding reported to G. When android draws the plain line for the object face it will collapse into this same pair and need its own row until styling lands.

entries.owner: E (SSoT) — ledger row; the implementation decision is under the orchestrator's adjudication
entries.reason: ios does not implement the gap half of distribution: equalSpacing and equalCentering both synthesise the same Spacer set, so the two values draw one picture — recorded as the ios row of attribute_semantics.json#semantics.distribution.collapsedPairs since run 3, re-measured on run 31068716186 (identical child positions, 32 px gap for both). android and web distinguish the pair (run-5 geometry: android gaps 26 vs 22, web 14 vs 12 with equalCentering's end half-gaps visible). This row is the fixture-side receipt of that known gap, not a new finding; it leaves this ledger together with the collapsedPairs row when ios implements the perValueMapping (Spacer-between-only vs half-spacers-at-ends). Implement-vs-defer for this release is under adjudication (E's proposal in 49-E-progress, 2026-08-06).
